title: arctostaphylos glandulosa subsp. adamsii
intro: Arctostaphylos glandulosa subsp. adamsii, commonly known as Bigberry Manzanita, is a species of flowering plant in the heath family (Ericaceae) that is native to the southwestern United States and Mexico. This plant has been traditionally used to support respiratory health, with its leaves and berries being used to make teas and infusions that help to alleviate coughs, colds, and other respiratory issues. The therapeutic actions of Bigberry Manzanita include expectorant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which contribute to its effectiveness in treating respiratory infections and promoting overall lung health. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities.
